profiles.summary: Arbitrum One still answers as the private build nitro v3.13.0-rc.9+b72783f on go1.27.3 and still runs ArbOS 61. Every rerun on 2026-11-25 matches the specification, and three new vector sets aimed at the jump destination bitmap, the shared stack arena of the go-ethereum fork and the Go issue 82839 shape match as well.

deltas.delta: The Security Council paused new Stylus activations on 2026-10-02, and a Constitutional AIP posted on 2026-10-23 would reopen them on Arbitrum One through an activation contract that lowers and restores the activation gas inside one transaction for code signed by the Arbitrum Foundation. Existing activated programs keep running. The PoolManager is EVM bytecode and is unaffected; only Stylus hooks and tokens that pool creators choose (F-003, F-053) gain a path back.

The OffchainLabs/go-ethereum master branch is older than the fork commit 0e44603 that Nitro v3.12.4 pins: its instructions.go still uses pop and peek where 0e44603 uses pop1Peek1 and a shared stack arena. The master branch is therefore not a candidate for the private rc.9 build.

profiles.summary: On 2026-10-30 the Security Council moved an account's ETH and ARB on Arbitrum One with unsigned transactions that named that account as sender, through a temporary Inbox implementation on Ethereum. The same path can name the PoolManager as sender through a contract transaction, which Nitro runs without nonce or EOA checks (new finding, governance level).

deltas.delta: Transactions of type 0x65 with zero signature fields and sender 0x3e2bf1ac6bf0934bbba6456c341c2ecbced632d5 were mined in blocks 519,514,683 and 519,514,685 and moved 74,559,805.2 ARB and 8,425.99 ETH to 0x...0da0, without the account's key.

profiles.summary: Native token management and transaction filtering are still off. The DAO is voting on new L1 pricing parameters for Glamsterdam, which change the L1 fee charged to users and nothing that a call returns.

deltas.delta: A Constitutional AIP sets parentGasFloorPerToken from 10 to 16 and perBatchGasCharge from 210,000 to 480,000 through ArbOwner once Glamsterdam is live on Ethereum, with no ArbOS change.

profiles.summary: No ArbOS upgrade is scheduled (getScheduledUpgrade returns zeros) and the network upgrades table lists nothing after ArbOS 61. The precompile scan from the PoolManager address was rerun.
Robinhood Chain answers as the same private rc.9 build, on amd64 in this cycle, and every rerun and new vector set matches the specification.

The chain's owners and rollup admin can produce a contract transaction from the PoolManager address in the same way as on Arbitrum One (same finding, operator and governance level). Nothing else is new.
Transaction filtering is still on since timestamp 1,782,295,200 (F-001) and native token management is off.
No ArbOS upgrade is scheduled, and the chain has two chain owners.

Elysium still answers as nitro/vlocal+unknown-unknown on go1.25.12 at ArbOS 61. Every rerun and new vector set matches the specification apart from script 189 of pmdiff2, the gas-capped swap seen in every earlier cycle.
No change. The single chain owner can produce a contract transaction from the PoolManager address through its own Inbox on HyperEVM (same finding).
Native token management and transaction filtering are off, and HYPE remains the native gas token.

The documentation now dates the HyperCore upgrade (a market data precompile and the ElysiumCoreWriter predeploy with callbacks paid from a gas escrow) to about four weeks after the 9 November 2026 mainnet. It is not scheduled on chain yet, and its addresses and ABIs are unpublished.

deltas.delta: The keeper lane of ElysiumCoreWriter will offer optional callbacks paid from a HYPE gas escrow, so the chain will call user contracts from a system path. Whether a callback runs as its own transaction, inside the transaction that emitted the intent, or in a frame that skips StateDB.Prepare is not documented.

findings.title: Arbitrum governance can post a contract transaction whose sender is the PoolManager, and Nitro runs it without a nonce or code check, so every pooled balance can be moved without unlock
findings.difference: On Ethereum only a key or the contract's own code can move what a contract holds. On Nitro chains the sender of an L1-to-L2 message is a field that the Inbox contract on the parent chain fills in, and the Inbox is upgradeable by the chain owner. On 2026-10-30 the Arbitrum Security Council (9 of 12, no delay on the emergency path) used a temporary Inbox implementation with sendUnsignedTransactionOverride to send two type 0x65 transactions from 0x3e2bf1ac6bf0934bbba6456c341c2ecbced632d5, which moved 74,559,805.2 ARB and 8,425.99 ETH. Nitro builds both unsigned user transactions and contract transactions with From set to the poster field of the message (arbos/parse_l2.go lines 245-269). The contract transaction type skips nonce checks and transaction checks (core/types/arb_types.go lines 66 and 77 of fork 0e44603), and the check that rejects a sender with code sits inside the transaction checks (core/state_transition.go preCheck), so a contract transaction may name an address that holds code.
findings.mechanism: An override Inbox would enqueue a message of kind ContractTx with the PoolManager address as sender, the address of a pooled token as destination and the calldata of transfer(recipient, balance), or a native value transfer with empty calldata. Nitro turns it into an ArbitrumContractTx from the PoolManager. Neither the nonce check nor the EOA check runs, so the call executes as an outer call whose msg.sender is the PoolManager. The token sees an ordinary transfer by its holder. Nothing in the PoolManager runs: no unlock, no delta accounting, no NonzeroDeltaCount check, so pools, positions and ERC-6909 claims still record balances that are gone. An eth_call from the PoolManager address to USDC with transfer(0x...0da0, whole balance) at block 527,417,705 returns true, which shows that the token itself places no hurdle on such a call. The type 0x65 path the Council used would fail for the PoolManager, because unsigned user transactions keep the EOA check (arb_types.go line 76); the contract transaction path does not. On Robinhood Chain the chain owners and the rollup admin on Ethereum hold the same path, and on Elysium the single chain owner and the Inbox admin on HyperEVM do.
findings.impact: Every balance the PoolManager holds on the three chains, which on Arbitrum One at block 527,417,705 includes 4,405.32 ETH and 9,252,963.77 USDC. Liquidity providers and claim holders of every pool would be left with records that cannot be paid out.
findings.preconditions: The Arbitrum Security Council emergency signers (9 of 12) or the DAO timelock on Arbitrum One, the chain owners or rollup admin on Robinhood Chain, or Elysium's owner. An ordinary account cannot reach it: the stock Inbox aliases the sender of every unsigned and contract message by adding 0x1111000000000000000000000000000000001111, and producing the PoolManager address would need control of a fixed parent chain address with no known key.
findings.mitigations: None in core. Integrators and LPs should treat these chains' upgrade path as able to spend any contract's balance, as the Binance freeze showed for an EOA. Off-chain monitors can watch for type 0x65 and 0x66 transactions whose sender is the PoolManager.

sources.supports: The Council upgraded the Inbox to add sendUnsignedTransactionOverride, impersonated the sender of two cross-chain transactions and restored the Inbox in one atomic action.
The Arbitrum One leg was transaction 0x75e81a... of type 0x65 with nonce 2 and zero signature fields.
Type 0x65 transactions 0x75e81a23...eeedb6 (ARB transfer to 0x...0da0) and 0x410af166...5f70 (ETH to 0x...0da0) from 0x3e2bf1ac...32d5 with r = 0.
UnsignedUserTx and ContractTx are built with From set to the message poster.
ArbitrumContractTx returns true from skipNonceChecks and skipTransactionChecks; ArbitrumUnsignedTx returns false for both.
Copy of the fork's core/state_transition.go read in cycle 16: the ErrSenderNoEOA check runs only when SkipTransactionChecks is false.

cleared.check: Jump destination analysis. codeBitmapInternal in core/vm/analysis_legacy.go:79 of fork 0e44603 decides whether a byte starts push data with the signed comparison int8(op) < int8(PUSH1), so opcodes 0x80 to 0xff are negative and skipped. 605 programs per chain put each of the 256 opcode bytes before a JUMPDEST at distances 0, 1, n-1, n and n+1 for PUSHn and jump to it.
cleared.result: All 605 programs give the specified outcome on each chain: the jump succeeds unless the JUMPDEST sits inside PUSHn data, and fails there. The analysis file is byte-identical in 0e44603 and on the fork's master. In the PoolManager bytecode 29 bytes of value 0x5b lie inside push data and no push constant names one as a target, so even a wrong bitmap could not redirect a jump in core.

cleared.check: Go issue 82839 (open; go1.26.6 to go1.26.10, go1.27.3 and master, a variant from go1.24.13): prove carries a fact through a sign extension of a narrow integer compared with a constant that does not fit the narrow type. Searched holiman/uint256 v1.3.2 (uint256.go, mod.go, div.go, conversion.go, decimal.go) and the fork's core/vm (memory.go, stack.go, instructions.go, interpreter.go, analysis_legacy.go, common.go) and core/state/transient_storage.go for conversions to int8, int16, int32, uint8, uint16 and uint32.
cleared.result: Four sites exist and none has the shape. analysis_legacy.go:79 compares two int8 values with the constant 96, which fits int8, and nothing is extended. uint256 ExtendSign (uint256.go:1275) computes uint64(int64(int8(signByte))) with no comparison or branch on the result. mod.go:53 compares a uint32 with 0x80000000, which fits uint32 and is zero-extended. The other uses are byte encodings in uint256.go:118 and 173. SIGNEXTEND, which TickMath and the int24 and int128 casts of the PoolManager depend on, passes 7,921 battery and 2,454 chained vectors on all three chains.

cleared.check: Shared stack arena of fork 0e44603 (core/vm/stack.go): one arena per EVM, each call frame starts at its parent's top, and stack() grows the slice with slices.Grow when fewer than 1,024 slots remain, while pop1Peek1 and pop2Peek1 hand out pointers into the slice. A parent that kept a pointer across a child call that grew the arena would read stale memory. Programs that push 2, 501 or 1,001 values, recurse to depth 0 to 8 so that every child forces a growth, and sum their own stack after the call.
cleared.result: 18 of 18 programs return (d+1)K(K+1)/2 on each chain and on Ethereum. opCall pops its operands by value and pushes its result through the arena pointer after the call (instructions.go:730-774), so no pointer survives a child frame. A PoolManager frame holds at most 49 items while it calls a hook or token, so the parent's values survive a hook or token that fills its own stack.

cleared.check: Rerun of precscan.py: P1 to P3 call shapes (empty calldata with value, balanceOf(PoolManager), transfer) from the PoolManager address at 336 precompile and system addresses, compared with cycle 16.
cleared.result: All 337 addresses (0x01 to 0x11f, 0x800 to 0x81f, 0xa4b000 to 0xa4b00f, 0xfffe, 0xffff) give byte for byte the code and the three answers recorded in cycle 16 on each chain, after retrying the Elysium rows that hit its rate limit. The only cross-chain differences are the five of cycle 16 (code at 0x65 and 0xc8, and the identity and SHA-256 precompiles echoing each chain's own PoolManager address), so no new system contract answers a take, sync or settle shape from the PoolManager (src/PoolManager.sol:279-297, src/types/Currency.sol:40-90).

cleared.check: Can an ordinary account get a parent chain message executed with the PoolManager as sender?
cleared.result: No. The stock Inbox passes every message sender through applyL1ToL2Alias in _deliverToBridge (Inbox.sol:317-324), so a contract or unsigned message with the PoolManager as sender needs a parent chain sender equal to the PoolManager address minus 0x1111000000000000000000000000000000001111, an address nobody holds a key or creation path for. The three ToFork functions undo the alias for an EOA caller, but they revert unless the parent chain id has changed, and the unsigned transaction they produce keeps the EOA check, which the PoolManager's code fails. Deposits credit the native balance without running code and are not a payment in settle, which reads msg.value (src/PoolManager.sol:349-364).

cleared.check: Upcoming forks for the next six months: scheduled ArbOS upgrades, DAO proposals and Orbit chain announcements, and what they change for the PoolManager.
cleared.result: No ArbOS version after 61 is proposed for Arbitrum One, and getScheduledUpgrade returns zeros on all three chains. The pending Arbitrum One actions are new L1 pricing parameters (no ArbOS change) and the Stylus activation contract, which changes nothing in the EVM interpreter and reaches the PoolManager only through Stylus hooks or tokens that pool creators choose. Robinhood Chain announces nothing. Elysium's HyperCore upgrade is announced and open as a lead.

leads.question: When the ElysiumCoreWriter predeploy ships, do its keeper callbacks run as separate transactions that pass through StateDB.Prepare, and can a callback target the PoolManager or a contract in the middle of another account's unlock?
leads.why: A callback executed inside another transaction's frame or without the transient storage reset would break A1 for the unlock flag and the synced currency (src/libraries/Lock.sol, src/libraries/CurrencyReserves.sol).

leads.question: When the Stylus Activation Contract source is published, can a call that lowers the activation gas be used, inside the same transaction, to activate a second program that was not signed?
leads.why: The proposal states the contract prevents this, but the code is unpublished; a gap would reopen activation of unaudited WASM hooks and tokens (F-003, F-053), which reach pools only by pool creator choice.

leadResults.answer: battery.py (99,985), targeted.py (85,544) and offsets.py (200) were rerun on 2026-11-25 against nitro v3.13.0-rc.9+b72783f go1.27.3 on Arbitrum One (arm64) and Robinhood Chain (amd64) with no mismatch. No public commit range contains b72783f: go.mod at v3.13.0, v3.13.0-rc.10, v3.13.1 and v3.12.5 returns 404 and proxy.golang.org reports b72783f as an unknown revision. The master CHANGELOG still ends at v3.11.0-rc.6 and links compare views of nitro-private.

The pin of rc.9 is still unreadable (same 404s and unknown revision on proxy.golang.org). The public fork master is older than 0e44603 and so not the source. The answers of the running build match the consensus-v61 behaviour on all reruns.

Elysium still reports nitro/vlocal+unknown-unknown/linux-amd64/go1.25.12. Its documentation says stock ArbOS 61 and names no source commit. All opcode, script, jump destination and stack arena vectors give the same answers as the rc.9 endpoints.

The call pattern probes of callsem.py (50 words, including transient storage rollback in reverted inner and outer frames, TSTORE under STATICCALL, value calls to empty accounts and failed call return data) give the specified words on Elysium and on Arbitrum One at ArbOS 61. The Elysium team still publishes no build commit.

Still no public endpoint serves the historical trace: arb1.arbitrum.io and publicnode do not expose debug_traceTransaction, drpc answers historical state is not available, and Tenderly's gateway answered rate limit exceeded (raw/l835_trace_probe.txt).

getScheduledUpgrade on Elysium still returns zeros at 2026-11-25. The documentation dates the HyperCore upgrade to about four weeks after the 9 November mainnet and still names no address or selector. precscan.py in this cycle's work directory is ready to rerun; a new lead covers the callback lane.

v3.13.0 is not tagged and b72783f is unknown to proxy.golang.org. Elysium's trace methods still need a key, so no step trace was possible; its answers match the rc.9 endpoints on every vector set of this cycle.
Operator level. No public challenger or watchtower for Robinhood Chain or Elysium was found and no Nitro binary is available here to replay batches.
The fork commit inside v3.13.0 is still unpublished. holiman/uint256 is v1.3.2 in both 0e44603 and the fork's master, and the endpoint answers match the specification.
